# orchestration_cluster_cluster_variable (Resource)

A variable inside a Camunda cluster, either global or scoped to a single tenant. See the Camunda documentation on [cluster variables](https://docs.camunda.io/docs/components/admin/cluster-variables/). The value is stored in the cluster's state and is **not** marked sensitive: do not store secrets in it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A global cluster variable. The value is a JSON document: use jsonencode().
resource "orchestration_cluster_cluster_variable" "global" {
  name  = "default-retries"
  value = jsonencode({ retries = 3 })
}

# A tenant-scoped cluster variable: set tenant_id.
resource "orchestration_cluster_cluster_variable" "tenant" {
  name      = "greeting"
  tenant_id = "my-tenant"
  value     = jsonencode("hello")
}

# A variable that references a secret, with metadata. The value holds the reference, not the secret.
resource "orchestration_cluster_cluster_variable" "secret_reference" {
  name  = "api-token"
  kind  = "SECRET_REFERENCE"
  value = jsonencode("camunda.secrets.API_TOKEN")

  metadata = {
    owner = "platform-team"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the cluster variable. Must be unique within its scope. Changing it replaces the variable.
- `value` (String) The value of the variable as a JSON document: any JSON object, array, string, number, boolean or `null`. Use `jsonencode()` to build it, e.g. `jsonencode("hello")` for the string `hello` or `jsonencode({ retries = 3 })` for an object. The value is stored exactly as configured; a value the API reports back in a different but JSON-equivalent form (whitespace, key order) does not cause a diff.

### Optional

- `kind` (String) The kind of the variable: `JSON` (the default) or `SECRET_REFERENCE`. A `SECRET_REFERENCE` variable may contain `camunda.secrets.<name>` references in its value, which are resolved when a job is activated, so the secret itself is never stored in the variable or in the Terraform state. The API cannot change the kind of an existing variable, so changing it replaces the variable.
- `metadata` (Map of String) Key-value metadata attached to the variable, at most 100 entries. The API also accepts numbers as metadata values; they are reported as their string representation. Omit it for no metadata.
- `tenant_id` (String) The ID of the tenant the variable belongs to. Omit it to create a global variable. Changing it (including adding or removing it) replaces the variable.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The identity of the variable, which is also its import ID: `GLOBAL/<name>` for a global variable or `TENANT/<tenant_id>/<name>` for a tenant-scoped one.
- `scope` (String) The scope of the variable: `GLOBAL` or `TENANT`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Global variable: GLOBAL/<name>
terraform import orchestration_cluster_cluster_variable.global "GLOBAL/default-retries"

# Tenant-scoped variable: TENANT/<tenant_id>/<name>
terraform import orchestration_cluster_cluster_variable.tenant "TENANT/my-tenant/greeting"
```
